title: lefagy, lemerül, elromlik: It Happens by Itself

sections.title: Things that happen to a thing
sections.content: You know from Unit 31 that some verbs describe something that simply happens to a thing, with nobody doing it: *elromlik* ("to break down") and *megoldódik* ("to get solved"). *lefagy* ("to freeze") and *lemerül* ("to run out of battery") do not end in *-ik*, but they work the same way: the device is the subject and nobody is blamed. A person who acts on the device uses a different verb with an object: *újraindít*, *frissít* or *megjavít* ("to fix", Unit 32).

sections.title: Key phrases
rows: I restart the computer (I do it).
The phone ran out of battery.

items.spanish: Lemerült a telefon, és lefagyott a számítógép.
items.english: The phone ran out of battery and the computer froze.

items.spanish: Elromlott a billentyűzet, ezért hívtam egy szerelőt.
items.english: The keyboard broke, so I called a technician.
My phone froze, so I restarted it.

sections.content: Do not make yourself the subject of a verb that describes the device. Say *Lefagyott a telefonom* ("my phone froze"), never *Lefagytam a telefonomat*. You act on the device with *újraindít*, *frissít* or *megjavít*.
